root.name: Benko Gambit: Fianchetto Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 b5 4. cxb5 a6 5. bxa6 Bxa6 6. Nc3 d6 7. Nf3 g6 8. g3

overview: In the Benko Gambit Accepted White declines to defend the extra pawn directly with a fianchetto set-up (g3, Bg2, O-O) and keeps it. Black has castled on the g-file with a Bg7 and rooks on the half-open a- and b-files, trying for long-term pressure on White's queenside. White tries to consolidate and return the pawn when useful.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with g3, Bg2 and castle, hold the extra pawn
Play Nd2, a4 and Ra2 or return the pawn to trade pieces

black_ideas.idea: Pressure on a- and b-files with rooks
Use the Bg7 on the long diagonal and ...Nbd7

typical_structures.structure: Benko structure with d5, e2/e4 against Black c5/d6
Half-open a- and b-files for Black

character.notes: Positional pressure for a pawn, slower than the main lines; not forced.

gambit.notes: Black has given a pawn on b5 and White can keep it.

structure.notes: Semi-open for Black's rooks on a- and b-files while White keeps a central wedge.

approach.notes: The Fianchetto is a main line of the Benko.

level.notes: Compensation is positional and needs good judgement.

plan_phrases: pressure on the a- and b-files

sublines_that_differ.name: 9.Bh3
sublines_that_differ.how: White removes the dark bishop battery.

character.reason: Positional pressure; sharper only when White returns the pawn badly.

gambit.reason: Black gives a pawn that White may keep.

soundness.reason: Benko is an anchor Sound gambit.

structure.reason: Half-open a- and b-files against a fixed d5 pawn.
